text: Gold slipped about 0.9% overnight to near $3,949, extending Wednesday's drop below $4,000, as the dollar index hit 103.08, its highest since April 2025, before easing to about 102.80.
Silver fell about 1% to near $51.04, so the gold/silver ratio held near 77.4.
Gold miners closed lower Wednesday with gold: GDX fell 1.48% to $85.21, GDXJ 1.68% to $104.51 and GDXU 4.58% to $82.51.
Treasury yields rose as trading resumed after Veterans Day: the 10-year is back at 5.01% (+2 bp) and the 2-year at 4.78% (+4 bp).

Nvidia fell about 6–8% premarket on reports its board is preparing to remove its CEO, and Nasdaq 100 futures were down about 0.9%, which points to a weaker start for QQQ and TQQQ and a stronger one for SQQQ.
Weekly jobless claims rose to 200,000, above the roughly 195,000 expected but still within their recent low range.
Brent eased about 0.6% to near $92.22 as higher OPEC+ output and a build in US crude stocks offset worries about mine strikes near the Strait of Hormuz; this matters for NRGU.
Bitcoin slipped to about $73,400 with tech stocks as US spot bitcoin ETFs had a fifth straight day of outflows, about $1.44 billion since Nov. 5.
